inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation (cash-flow add-back), CIK0000008670, FY2026 10-K (period 2025-07-01/2026-06-30) = $242.6M; matches ADP_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp. ADP does not separately disclose cash tax withheld on net-share settlement (low-SBC filer, ~1.1% of revenue, no PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation tag found in companyfacts); sbc_incl_equity_taxes therefore equals the cash-flow add-back only -- immaterial given SBC's small scale relative to revenue.
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted weighted-average for the quarter ended 2026-09-30, Q1 FY2027 10-Q income statement = 397.6M (basic 396.5M + 1.1M options/RSUs), down from 403.3M for FY2026 -- same basis as the prior build. The 10-Q cover shows 394.8M basic shares at 2026-10-27; that later count is NOT used because the October repurchases that produced it are not in the 30 September cash balance, and pairing the two would count the buyback twice. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the owner-FCF build, so charging both the SBC expense and a rising count would double-count. ADP is a genuine repurchaser funding the flat count: $758.8M of repurchases in Q1 FY2027 alone (vs $366.0M in Q1 FY2026), $2,476.1M trailing twelve months.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.5% for a large-cap, investment-grade (A-rated), low-beta (~0.9), highly recurring-revenue US services business. Built from a ~4.2% risk-free rate (10-year UST, Sep-2026) plus a ~4.8% levered ERP given ADP's very high revenue retention (~92% Employer Services) and mature capital structure; consistent with peers in the payroll/HCM space (Paychex, comparable large-cap software/services names run 8-9.5%).
inputs.lease_treatment: not material -- ADP's operating leases (office space) are small relative to the balance sheet and cash flows; no separate lease adjustment applied (US company, section 7 adaptations not triggered).
inputs.nci_treatment: none -- ADP has no reported noncontrolling interests.
inputs.notes: UPDATE 2026-11-19 (prior build 2026-09-25). Model unchanged: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year horizon; no MEMORY.md entry for ADP, routing re-confirmed against dcf-methods/SKILL.md (operating company; client-funds float is a pass-through, not a deposit book). REFRESHED: price; cash, debt and diluted share count to the Q1 FY2027 10-Q (quarter ended 2026-09-30); buyback pace to TTM. RE-JUDGED (year 1 = FY2027 only): (1) bull year-1 growth 9.0% -> 7.0% and bear year-1 growth 3.0% -> 4.5%: Q1 revenue grew 6.1% ($5,490.7M vs $5,175.2M) and management raised the FY2027 guide to ~6% (from 5-6%) on 2026-10-28, so with one quarter banked neither 9% nor 3% for the full year is reachable without an implausible swing in the remaining three quarters. Base year-1 growth stays 6.0% -- it already sat on the raised guide. (2) Base year-1 EBITDA margin 27.3% -> 27.6% and bear 26.0% -> 26.5%: on this model's own basis (pre-tax earnings + D&A - other income) Q1 was 26.8% vs 26.0% a year earlier, +80bps, and adjusted EBIT margin was +130bps against an unchanged +70-90bps full-year guide; FY2026's 26.9% also carried the $91.1M business-alignment charge (0.4pt). Bull year-1 margin 27.8% unchanged. (3) Base and bull year-1 SBC 1.10% -> 1.15% of revenue: Q1 SBC was $67.2M, 1.22% of revenue, +14% year on year. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: FY0 stays FY2026 (base revenue $21,947.4M, owner FCF $4,162.5M = reported FCF $4,776.1M - SBC $242.6M - corporate interest income $371.0M) because Q1 is seasonally the weakest cash quarter and a TTM rebase would add noise, not information. Growth, margin, SBC, D&A, capex and tax paths for years 2-10 in all three scenarios; WACC 8.5/8.0/10.0; terminal growth and cap multiples; working-capital capture; scenario weights 20/50/30. Q1 capex + capitalised software was $169.8M = 3.1% of revenue against a 3.0% path, and FY2027 PP&E capex is guided $200-225M: consistent, no change. Q1 effective tax rate 22.7% against a 23.0% path: no change. What would move them: a change to the 70-90bps margin guide or a second quarter of >100bps expansion (margin path years 2-3); a client-funds interest guide below $1.59-1.61B or a Fed path that pulls the average yield under ~3.3% (bear weight and bear margins); bookings growth outside the 4-7% guide or retention falling by more than the guided 10-30bps (growth path years 2-4); a 10-year UST move of more than ~50bps from the ~4.2% the WACC was built on. OPEN METHOD QUESTION, NOT CHANGED HERE: the EBITDA margin basis inherited from the prior build is pre-tax earnings + D&A - other income, i.e. it is AFTER all $459.3M of FY2026 interest expense and BEFORE all $371.0M of corporate interest income. Two things follow. The ~$5.0B of senior notes is charged twice -- their interest is inside the flows and their principal is deducted as net debt. And most of the stripped interest income is earned on borrowed funds in the client-funds extended investment strategy (average corporate investments $10.4B in FY2026 and $13.9B in Q1 FY2027, against $3-4B of balance-sheet cash), whose borrowing cost stays in the flows while the income does not. ADP's own adjusted EBIT (26.8% FY2026 margin) keeps client-funds-strategy interest income and expense and excludes the rest; on that basis FY2026 EBITDA margin is roughly 29.5% rather than 26.9%. Both effects understate value; rough size +$15-25/share on the base case (unverified -- it needs the notes-interest and corporate-cash-interest split from the 10-K debt note). Left as is so this update stays comparable with the prior build; it should be decided as a deliberate methodology change with its own bridge line. CARRIED FROM PRIOR BUILD: capex = PP&E + additions to intangibles (FY2026 $196.6M + $468.5M = $665.1M), excluding M&A; cash tax rate flat at 23% (effective rate 22.5-23.2% for eight years); 10-year horizon because margin is still on a guided upward path.
inputs.buyback_cash_note: Trailing twelve months to 2026-09-30: FY2026 $2,083.3M - Q1 FY2026 $366.0M + Q1 FY2027 $758.8M = $2,476.1M (10-Q cash flow statement, 'Repurchases of common stock'). Pace has roughly doubled year on year under the $6B authorisation of January 2026.
inputs.net_debt_note: Q1 FY2027 10-Q balance sheet at 2026-09-30: cash and cash equivalents $3,277.0M; long-term debt $4,965.3M + current portion $14.8M = $4,980.1M; net debt $1,703.1M (was $735.0M at 2026-06-30). The $968M increase is the quarter's buybacks ($758.8M) and dividends ($677.0M) exceeding seasonally weak Q1 operating cash flow ($651.0M). No commercial paper outstanding at either date. Client funds assets/obligations and the reverse-repo borrowings that fund them remain outside net debt, as before.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr, moderated toward FY2027 guidance midpoint (5-6%)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Shareholders' equity CAGR is not usable here: ADP is an aggressive repurchaser whose book value swung from a $679.8M DEFICIT (FY2018) to $6,031.2M (FY2026) purely on buyback/dividend timing versus retained earnings, so equity CAGR (19.8% 3yr / 1.2% 5yr) is an artifact of the buyback cadence, not of the underlying business. Owner-FCF CAGR (8.4% 3yr / 11.9% 5yr, on the SBC- and interest-income-adjusted series) and revenue CAGR (6.8% 3yr / 7.9% 5yr) are the reliable anchors; selected_growth_rate uses revenue, moderated to management's own FY2027 guidance (5-6%) rather than the higher historical average, since FY2026's 7% growth was flagged by management itself as a strong year the FY2027 guide is normalizing down from.
historical_growth.notes: Unchanged from the 2026-09-25 build: CAGRs are computed on fiscal years through FY2026 and one further quarter does not move them. Q1 FY2027 revenue growth was 6.1% and diluted EPS growth 14%.

base.narrative: FY2027 guidance as raised on 2026-10-28 (~6% revenue growth, +70-90bps adjusted EBIT margin, adjusted EPS +10-12%, client-funds interest $1.59-1.61B) decelerating gradually toward a long-run ~3.5-4%. Year-1 margin lifted to 27.6% after Q1 ran +80bps year on year on this model's basis; years 2-10 are the prior path, ramping to ~29.5% as AI Assist efficiency, Lyric HCM scale and a growing high-margin client-funds interest mix compound. Capex stays ~3% of revenue (Q1: 3.1%) on continued software capitalisation. Cash tax rate flat at 23% (Q1 effective rate 22.7%).

bull.narrative: Year-1 growth cut to 7.0% (from 9.0%): with Q1 at 6.1% and the guide at ~6%, the bull case for FY2027 is a modest beat, not a re-acceleration; the above-guidance growth now starts in year 2. Thereafter unchanged: AI Assist delivers efficiency faster and deeper than guided, record Employer Services bookings and Lyric HCM enterprise momentum sustain 7-8.5% growth, client-funds interest outgrows guidance on balances and yield, and retention holds at ~92% against Paychex-Paycor, Rippling and Dayforce. Margin expands toward 32%.

bear.narrative: Year-1 growth raised to 4.5% (from 3.0%) and year-1 margin to 26.5% (from 26.0%): one quarter at 6.1% growth and +80bps margin is banked, so the bear case for FY2027 is a second-half fade rather than a full-year stall. Thereafter unchanged: the Fed cuts faster and deeper than expected, reversing the client-funds interest tailwind (now guided $1.59-1.61B, ~7% of revenue); Paychex-Paycor scale and cloud-native entrants erode bookings and pricing in the mid-market; the Lyric migration costs more than it saves near term. Growth stalls near 2%, margin compresses before AI efficiency partly offsets it late in the horizon.

scenario_narratives.base: Raised FY2027 guide (~6% revenue, +70-90bps adjusted EBIT margin, EPS +10-12%) decelerating gradually to a mature ~3.5-4%; margin ramps to ~29.5% on AI efficiency, Lyric HCM scale and a growing high-margin client-funds interest mix.
scenario_narratives.bull: FY2027 a modest beat of the ~6% guide, then AI-driven efficiency and Lyric HCM enterprise wins sustain above-guidance growth; client-funds interest outgrows the guide; retention holds despite Paychex-Paycor and cloud-native competition.
scenario_narratives.bear: A second-half FY2027 fade, then a faster/deeper Fed cutting cycle reverses the client-funds interest tailwind while competitive and platform-migration pressure slows bookings and compresses margin before AI efficiency can offset it.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default nudged toward bear (20% vs 15% default) because ADP's own risk disclosure names interest-rate-cycle exposure as a HIGH-severity financial and macro risk simultaneously -- a rate-cutting cycle is a real, identifiable near-term catalyst (not a generic risk) that would compress a high-margin, fast-growing revenue line the base case leans on for margin expansion. Bull trimmed to 30% because it requires several things to go right together (AI efficiency ahead of guidance, Lyric HCM momentum sustaining, AND a still-favorable rate/yield environment) rather than one clean catalyst. UNCHANGED at this update (2026-11-19): the Q1 beat and guide raise were driven largely by client-funds interest, which sharpens rather than relieves the rate exposure the 20% bear weight is there for.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ADP is valued as a mature, highly recurring, capital-light services compounder with an unusual (for a services company) interest-rate-sensitive revenue stream layered on top of the core payroll/HCM business. The valuation is built on owner FCF (SBC and corporate interest income stripped, share count held flat since buybacks are the funding mechanism for that flat count) over a 10-year horizon because margins are still on a genuine, management-guided upward path rather than already mature. Client funds interest revenue is treated as ordinary, already-embedded revenue -- not modeled as a bank's net interest margin -- because ADP does not take credit risk on the funds; the float asset and obligation net to zero in net debt.
key_risks_to_valuation: Client funds interest revenue reversal if the Fed cuts rates faster/further than guided -- this is the single largest swing factor between scenarios
Competitive share loss to Paychex-Paycor (larger combined scale), Rippling, Dayforce and Paylocity in the mid-market
Multi-year Lyric HCM platform migration execution risk for large enterprise clients
Cybersecurity/data-breach exposure given the sensitive payroll and personal data ADP holds for tens of millions of workers
US employment levels and small-business formation rates drive the underlying payroll/PEO volume the model assumes keeps growing
